findings.claim: AC (vii) 7-day staleness check is missing from the aggregator. DISPATCH-NOTE AC (vii) explicitly specifies four failure conditions, one of which is 'no green run within last 7 days' triggering status: no_emit. The implementation fetches createdAt from gh run list (included in --json databaseId,headSha,createdAt) but NEVER compares it against a 7-day window. The --limit 1 call returns the most recent successful run regardless of age; a run from 6 months ago is accepted as current data.
findings.evidence: scorecard-aggregator.yml Python heredoc lines 135-170: gh run list call uses '--json databaseId,headSha,createdAt' but the parsed result only reads latest.get('databaseId') and latest.get('headSha'). The createdAt value is never extracted or compared. The no_emit path (line 165-169) triggers only when runs is empty (no successful run ever), not when the most recent run is older than 7 days. DISPATCH-NOTE AC (vii): 'emit signature invalid OR unreachable adopter OR no green run within last 7 days OR schema-invalid emit → adopter row records the failure-mode + error string; aggregator does NOT silently drop.' The 7-day condition is a named acceptance criterion, not aspirational text.
findings.impact: An adopter who has not run policy-check in weeks or months will have their stale data included in the index as if it is current. The aggregated_at timestamp on the index indicates when the AGGREGATION ran, not when the adopter's emit was produced. Operator and MCP consumers reading the index will not know that some adopter rows are months out of date unless they inspect last_emit_emitted_at per adopter. The plan-doc invariant 1 requires the aggregator to 'faithfully report verified emit content' — passing through a months-old emit without staleness flagging undermines the freshness signal the index is meant to provide.
findings.mitigation: After fetching the latest run, add a staleness check: parse latest.get('createdAt') as a datetime and compare against datetime.now(tz=timezone.utc) - timedelta(days=7). If older than 7 days, record row['status'] = 'no_emit' and row['error'] = f'most recent green policy-check run is {age_days}d old (threshold: 7d); no fresh emit available'. This is a ~5-line addition to the Python heredoc. Alternatively, file TF-023C-003 and amend DISPATCH-NOTE AC (vii) to remove the 7-day condition if the design intent is to accept any-age run — but the current AC is explicit and the omission should be a deliberate decision, not a silent gap.

findings.claim: The commit job opens a PR with branch name scorecards/${{ github.run_id }} and title 'chore(scorecards): weekly aggregator run ${{ github.run_id }}', but DISPATCH-NOTE AC (vi) explicitly specifies scorecards/<YYYY-MM-DD> and 'chore(scorecards): weekly aggregator run <YYYY-MM-DD>'. The deviation is systematic — run_id replaces date in both the branch name and PR title.
findings.evidence: scorecard-aggregator.yml commit job, peter-evans/create-pull-request step: 'branch: scorecards/${{ github.run_id }}' and 'title: "chore(scorecards): weekly aggregator run ${{ github.run_id }}"'. DISPATCH-NOTE AC (vi): 'commits on a scorecards/<YYYY-MM-DD> branch; pushes branch; opens a PR titled chore(scorecards): weekly aggregator run <YYYY-MM-DD> for operator review.' The date format is specified verbatim in the AC.
findings.impact: Branch names and PR titles carry run_id (an opaque integer) rather than the human-readable date. The operator reviewing the queue of aggregator PRs cannot tell at a glance which date each run corresponds to; they must cross-reference the run_id against the Actions log. Using run_id avoids branch collision on multiple same-day runs (e.g. workflow_dispatch triggered after the weekly cron), which is arguably better design — but this design difference should be reconciled with the AC rather than left as a silent deviation. The PR body does not include the aggregation date either (it includes the run_id link but not a formatted date).
findings.mitigation: Option A (align with AC): change branch and title to use $(date -u +%Y-%m-%d) or pass the date as a job output from the aggregate job, using scorecards/<YYYY-MM-DD>-${{ github.run_id }} to retain collision-safety. Option B (amend AC): update DISPATCH-NOTE AC (vi) to ratify the run_id convention and document why run_id is preferred over date (collision-safe, traceable to the exact Actions run). Either option closes the spec/implementation divergence. Option B is preferred if multiple same-day runs via workflow_dispatch are expected.

findings.claim: Plan-doc §5 specifies that when an adopter is unreachable, 'row from the prior index is retained.' The implementation does NOT retain the prior row — it writes a fresh index with status: unreachable and the adopter's last-known-good data is lost. D-042 does not explicitly note this deviation from plan-doc §5.
findings.evidence: Plan-doc §5 Failure modes: 'Adopter repo unreachable (rate-limit, deletion) → adopter row marked unreachable_at: <ts>; row from the prior index is retained.' scorecard-aggregator.yml Python heredoc: when gh run list or gh run download fails, row['status'] = 'unreachable' and row['error'] = ... The aggregator then builds a fresh index from the in-memory adopter_rows and calls INDEX_PATH.write_text(json.dumps(index,...)) — there is no step that reads the existing index.json to merge retained rows. D-042 row in DECISIONS.md does not mention the prior-row-retention behavior or its absence.
findings.impact: For a temporarily unreachable adopter, the operator loses last-known-good data (verdict, rule_counts, waivers_aggregate, scp_version) for the duration of the outage. The markdown report generator (023D) will show empty data for that adopter rather than the last verified state. If the operator is using the scorecard to track compliance drift, an unreachable adopter creates a data gap that looks like a fresh no_emit rather than a temporary network issue. D-042 implicitly overrides the plan-doc §5 behavior (DISPATCH-NOTE AC (vii) only mentions recording failure modes, not retention), but the deviation is not acknowledged.
findings.mitigation: Option A (implement retention): before building the fresh index, read the existing index.json (if present) and for each adopter with a non-verified new result, merge in the prior row under a prior_row sub-key (or retain the prior data with a staleness flag). This is ~10 lines of Python. Option B (document deviation): amend D-042 to explicitly state 'Prior-row retention from plan-doc §5 is NOT implemented at v0.1 — the aggregator writes a fresh index each run; an unreachable adopter loses its last-known-good data until the next successful aggregation.' and add TF-023C-003 for prior-row-retention as a 023D or 023E enhancement. Option B is the appropriate 023C response since retention adds complexity; the deviation should be acknowledged rather than silently present.

findings.claim: The expected_scp_workflow_ref regex pattern in schemas/scorecard-opt-in-registry.schema.json allows any owner/repo prefix, not just jrnb2024/standards-control-plane/. A misconfigured (or adversarial) registry entry could pass schema validation while referencing a workflow that is NOT the SCP reusable workflow. The aggregator passes expected_scp_workflow_ref verbatim to gh attestation verify --signer-workflow, so a wrong path would verify against the wrong workflow's attestation.
findings.evidence: schemas/scorecard-opt-in-registry.schema.json expected_scp_workflow_ref pattern: '^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/\.github/workflows/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+\.ya?ml@[0-9a-f]{40}$'. This allows jrnb2024/standards-control-plane/.github/workflows/policy-check.yml@<sha> (correct) but also attacker-org/forked-repo/.github/workflows/fake-check.yml@<sha> (incorrect). DISPATCH-NOTE IN table: 'schemas/scorecard-opt-in-registry.schema.json ... each entry carries expected_scp_workflow_ref: jrnb2024/standards-control-plane/.github/workflows/policy-check.yml@<sha> (the SCP reusable workflow path + SHA pin the adopter’s caller wrapper invokes).' The schema description field describes intent but the pattern field does not enforce the owner/repo prefix.
findings.impact: An adopter who accidentally omits the trailing dash (registering jrnb2024/standards-control-plane/.github/workflows/policy-check.yml@<sha> instead of jrnb2024/standards-control-plane/...) would pass schema validation but get verification_failure on every aggregator run without an obvious error. More seriously, a future adopter registry PR could register a non-SCP workflow ref. In single-operator count=0 mode (D-033), the operator self-reviews registry PRs without a second approver — a momentary lapse could merge a misconfigured entry. The schema pattern is the machine-enforceable safeguard for registry correctness.
findings.mitigation: Tighten the pattern to: '^jrnb2024/standards-control-plane/\.github/workflows/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+\.ya?ml@[0-9a-f]{40}$'. This pins the owner and repo to the canonical SCP path while keeping the filename and SHA generic (allows future workflow renames like policy-check-v2.yml). The pattern should also add a forward-looking comment explaining that if the SCP repo is ever moved to an org, this pattern is the one field that needs a schema version bump + migration.

findings.claim: The adopter wrapper naming constraint (wrapper workflow file must be named policy-check.yml) is not documented in the opt-in-registry.yaml header, DISPATCH-NOTE adoption guide, or any adopter-facing documentation. The aggregator hardcodes --workflow policy-check.yml in the gh run list call. An adopter whose wrapper is named ci.yml, build.yml, or anything other than policy-check.yml will receive no_emit status with a confusing error message.
findings.evidence: scorecard-aggregator.yml line 140: '"--workflow", "policy-check.yml"' is hardcoded. docs/scorecards/opt-in-registry.yaml header: 4-step opt-in guide (bump SHA pin, set scorecard-emit: true, open PR, await merge) — no mention of wrapper file naming requirement. DISPATCH-NOTE IN table: aggregator script 'gh run list --workflow policy-check.yml --branch <default_branch> --status success --limit 1'. The SCP self-dogfood wrapper is named policy-check-wrapper.yml (not policy-check.yml), which means if the SCP repo dogfoods via TF-023C-001, the aggregator would return no_emit for the SCP repo itself unless the search is changed.
findings.impact: An adopter with a wrapper named anything other than policy-check.yml will appear as no_emit in the index. The error message 'no green policy-check.yml run found on default branch' will be confusing — the adopter knows they have green runs, just not named that. This is a usability gap that could block Threshold A onboarding (023E) if FLA or another pilot adopter has a differently-named wrapper. The SCP self-dogfood scenario (TF-023C-001) specifically would fail if the self-test wrapper remains named policy-check-wrapper.yml.
findings.mitigation: Option A (document the constraint): add to opt-in-registry.yaml header step 1.5: 'Your wrapper workflow that calls the SCP reusable workflow MUST be named policy-check.yml (this is what the aggregator queries via gh run list --workflow policy-check.yml).' Also add a schema description note on the adopter item. Option B (make the constraint configurable): add an optional workflow_filename field to the registry schema (default: policy-check.yml) and use it in the gh run list call. This removes the hardcoded constraint and accommodates adopters with differently-named wrappers. Option B is the more robust long-term fix; Option A is appropriate for 023C if Option B is deferred as TF-023C-004.

findings.claim: Plan-doc invariant 6 ('Aggregator output is Ed25519-signed') and plan-doc §4 threat model ('the index itself carries an Ed25519 signature over its full content; consumers verify before trusting') are now stale relative to D-042's actual trust model (git-history + CODEOWNERS + branch protection). A future reader of the plan-doc will encounter conflicting descriptions of how the index is trusted.
findings.evidence: WP-SCP-023 plan-doc §2 invariant 6: 'Aggregator output is Ed25519-signed. Each emit + the central index carry an Ed25519 signature using the same key infrastructure WP-SCP-021 established for MCP receipts.' Plan-doc §4 threat model (boundary 3): 'Threat: a tampered index could mis-report estate state. Mitigation: the index itself carries an Ed25519 signature over its full content; consumers verify before trusting.' D-042: 'index trust rooted in git’s required-signed-commits (slice 020J) + output/scorecards/** @jrnb2024 CODEOWNERS coverage + branch protection on main (slice 020D2), NOT a separate Ed25519 key layer.' The D-042 reframing is well-reasoned (Sigstore/Fulcio uses Ed25519 under the hood; git history is signed; CODEOWNERS gates every index-touching PR) and acceptable, but the plan-doc body was not updated to reflect it.
findings.mitigation: Add a plan-doc amendment note at §2 invariant 6: '(Amended by D-042: the in-payload Ed25519 signature described here was superseded — see D-042 for the actual trust model rationale: Sigstore/Fulcio OIDC for per-emit trust; git required-signed-commits + CODEOWNERS + branch protection for index trust.)' Similarly amend §4 boundary 3's mitigation text. This is a 2-sentence documentation fix. Alternatively, add a plan-doc version 0.2 amendment block noting which invariants are D-042-superseded.

summary: 15 ACs evaluated; 13 substantively met, 1 MAJ gap (AC vii — 7-day staleness check missing), 2 partial (AC vi branch naming deviation; AC xi STATUS.md tracked-forward section missing). D-042 is complete and accurate on all four required elements: (a) --signer-workflow mandatory constraint, (b) git-rooted index trust not separate Ed25519 layer, (c) two-job permission split, (d) bus-factor-1 acknowledged. The gh attestation verify invocation correctly uses both --signer-workflow and --repo (adopter repo, not SCP repo). Plan-doc §6 deliverables substantially match: workflow, registry, registry schema, index schema, placeholder index, README, D-042, VERSIONING.md extension, STATUS.md row all present. Risk rows R-023-02 (OIDC + git trust), R-023-03 (opt-in-only registry), R-023-05 (workflow_dispatch fallback), R-023-06 (bus-factor-1 in D-042), R-023-08 (schema const v0.1 enforces version drop) are all addressed. The D-042 reframing of invariant 6 (Ed25519-in-spirit via Sigstore/Fulcio + git required-signed-commits) is acceptable as a governance decision; the plan-doc text is stale (nit) but D-042 explicitly supersedes it. The expected_scp_workflow_ref regex is too permissive (any owner/repo allowed); tightening to jrnb2024/standards-control-plane/ prefix is the correct fix. Cross-repo notification (TF-023A-002) correctly deferred to 023D — no adopter onboarding path exists at 023C scope. Self-dogfood (TF-023C-001) correctly deferred; 023C's correctness does not depend on SCP opting in. Memory update items and rate-limit TF are nit-level housekeeping gaps. Verdict: CHANGES_REQUESTED — one MAJ (7-day staleness check) blocks approval; all MIN/nit items are either inline-fixable or TF-filings that do not block the PR.
